entries.title: Derwent Water's high E. coli results: diagnosis and a lake seasonal response
entries.verdict: By the plan's rule, Derwent Water's results over 900 are not explained by recorded spills at its three monitored overflows upstream: 30-day spill hours ranked its counts with rho 0.28 (interval −0.19 to +0.58), its overflows spilled less in its worst season (172 hours) than in 2024 (220), and 1 of its 4 dry-day results over 900 had a recorded spill in the 7 days before. At Coniston Water recorded spills did track counts (7-day rho 0.48, interval +0.27 to +0.62). Derwent's counts rose with water temperature and day of season (rho 0.37, interval +0.15 to +0.56). A lake-specific seasonal response (candidate D) failed all three of its conditions. Low lake level at Lodore did not track its results either (rho −0.12, interval −0.48 to +0.36); outflow at Portinscale could not be judged because the EA holds no 2024-25 flow there.
entries.scope: Derwent Water at Crow Park, 40 samples in 2024-25 for recorded spills (no 2026 event records) and 59 in 2024-26 for temperature, with Coniston Water and Windermere for comparison; seen samples, described. entries.title: River rises from upstream gauges, radar and the gauge's own history
entries.verdict: Failed as stated, run 5 to 6 November 2026 on 33 spot gauges in 13 river systems (hindcast, archived 15-minute series, 20 November 2024 to 24 October 2026). C1 (upstream gauges added to the spot gauge's own trend): Brier skill 0.0199, 95% interval −0.1849 to 0.0723, labelled "Too uncertain"; worse when read three hours late (−0.0617, "Possible harm"). C2 (radar added): skill against C1 0.0415, interval 0.0017 to 0.0826, below the 0.05 needed, hit rate 0.115 at the 0.5 line; labelled "Better" against C1 only, with no shown gain over the spot's own trend. Median lead gained 1 h on 100 of 677 onsets. The base rate by gauge and month ranked the next three hours best (AUC 0.815). 119 EA requests, all within the caps. entries.title: Satellite lake readings: the images behind the shore-margin outliers, and a sensitivity flag
entries.verdict: Exploratory, 26 selected scenes read (118 requests, 72.3 MiB) plus the second sample's 50. The 0.23 Serpentine shift and both Lake District outliers are scenes where the water's B4 and B5 reflectance is a few thousandths (inner B4 0.0005, B5 0.0007 to 0.0025), so the index is a ratio of noise and the brighter one-pixel shore rim steers the median; not a shore bloom, bottom or mask-width effect. Pre-stated pair test: 5 of 5 big same-day pairs have their extreme scene dark or spread, 1 of 4 small pairs flagged. entries.title: Satellite lake readings: quality-aware chlorophyll candidates against the lab chlorophyll baseline
entries.verdict: Development on seen 2021-2026 pairs, not fresh confirmation. 183 of 207 paired scenes read (803 requests, 418.4 MiB; the fetch ended on a second dropped connection, as pre-stated). Out-of-fold skill gain over #386's baseline on held-out lakes: A, low-signal readings excluded, +0.143 [+0.005, +0.306] at 81% coverage; C, brightness and pixel spread as covariates, +0.137 [+0.034, +0.233]; both keep the direction on held-out seasons and forward years, so both meet the pre-stated bar for a shadow log. B, weighting by a fitted noise model, +0.017 [−0.066, +0.139], is not supported; D, a per-pixel brightness floor, +0.034 [−0.122, +0.178], is inconclusive (its lower end is beyond the −0.05 harm margin). E, a three-day composite, was not tested. The lake's own training mean scores higher than every candidate on held-out seasons and years.
entries.scope: 38 EA chlorophyll monitoring points, May to September 2021-2026, samples with a usable scene within a day.
